item.title: Judge halts construction of Trump's arch. And, Labor Department to release jobs report
item.description: A judge has blocked construction of Trump's arch moments after it won federal approval to proceed. And, the Labor Department is set to release the latest jobs report today, a day after stocks plunged.
item.content:encoded:

item.title: Why gold prices are surprisingly low
item.description: Gold tends to go up when there's uncertainty in the economy. For a while, the price reflected that. But this week, it dropped from a nearly $5,600 in January to below $4,000. What's going on?

item.title: Past White House adviser Raj Panjabi has written a playbook for 'living room' crises
item.description: Dr. Raj Panjabi is the author of Safer: A Playbook. His goal is to help people face a personal crisis — health, workplace, family conflicts — and "turn fear into action."

item.title: Low birth rates were emptying public schools. ICE deportations are now making it worse
item.description: School enrollment was already expected to plunge by 2 million kids by 2030. Education experts say deporting immigrant families, many with school-age children, is making the crisis worse.

item.title: Former Army medic reflects on his toughest moments helping the wounded
item.description: Twenty years ago, Army Staff Sergeant Phillip Trezza deployed to Iraq as a medic. He speaks with his teenage daughter about some of his toughest moments.

item.title: After cancer surgery, Pope Leo embarks on Latin America trip
item.description: Pope Leo XIV is kicking off a three-nation tour of Latin America with a visit to Uruguay, three weeks after undergoing lung cancer surgery that had put the entire trip into question.

item.title: A judge blocks construction of Trump's arch moments after it won federal approval
item.description: The Trump administration hoped to begin construction immediately after a federal panel approved its arch late Thursday. But just after midnight, the judge issued an order blocking work for 14 days.
item.content:encoded:
The Trump administration hoped to begin construction immediately after a federal panel approved its arch late Thursday. But just after midnight, the judge issued an order blocking work for 14 days.

(Image credit: Tom Brenner)

item.title: Fears of an AI crackdown after midterms spark $2 trillion rout in tech stocks
item.description: Shares sank, with the tech-heavy Nasdaq dropping over 5%, as investors reacted with fear that a Democratic Congress — and states across the country -— would crack down on AI and data centers.
